correctness.rationale: All 65,535 nonempty Boolean four-variable teams are enumerated exactly. The direct quantified recombination semantics and an independent fibre-rectangularity implementation agree on 1,572,840 team/atom pairs. Complete profile grouping gives 1,342 signatures, with a ten-row maximum minimum witness attained by 28 signatures. The explicit S4 permutation action gives 125 orbits. All announced distributions, canonical witnesses, and CSV counts are asserted and reproducibly verified in checker.cpp; claims are finite only.

evidence: Šimeček studies probabilistic conditional-independence structures of four discrete random variables, reporting the count 18,478 in that different representability class, with no bound on four binary team support witnesses.

The Abramsky–Puljujärvi–Väänänen work explicitly compares relational and probabilistic team notions; neither displayed abstract nor inspected semantics suggests that their results imply the finite 1,342-profile classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A result on all probabilistically realizable independence models does not by itself count those realized by binary supports under every simultaneous relational atom: statistical factorization is not the same semantic condition as Cartesian support, and arbitrary discrete domains do not impose the Boolean 16-assignment universe. No more general theorem with a stated specialization yielding these counts was identified.

originality.rationale: The 2011/2012 team-semantics paper defines the relational independence atom, and the 2006 probabilistic conditional-independence model paper treats the same four named variable positions but with statistical/discrete representability, not Boolean relational supports. The 2026 finite-atom sequent-calculus source gives proof theory, not the exact support-team census in accessible published material. The 1,342, 125, 28 and sharp ten-team figures were compared by exact claim/implication against these sources and targeted mathematical searches; no covering theorem or table was identified. An unindexed binary-relational census is a residual historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: A historic, unindexed enumeration of binary relational conditional-independence types on four attributes could reproduce the precise classification.
The full text of the June 2026 sequent-calculus source was not accessible, so no whole-document NOT_COVERING claim is made; its accessible scope is not directly this enumeration.
The calculations are strictly for exactly four Boolean variables and 24 elementary pairwise conditioned atoms; extension to larger domains or probabilistic independence is not asserted.

value.rationale: The exact full 24-atom Boolean team-independence spectrum is an intrinsic finite representation invariant. Besides the total profile and orbit counts, the sharp universal ten-assignment realization bound and 28 extremal signatures distinguish what can and cannot be realized on smaller teams. This complete motivated classification and downloadable witness database are not routine normalization or an arbitrary isolated instance, and may support finite-variable entailment/representation studies.
